Start with a question: six reading paths

Editorial starting points, not rankings or required courses. Each link opens its listing below, with access, context and limits. Starting-point links clear active filters.

Learn the game

Start with the deal, check hand rankings, then work through a lesson.

  1. Texas hold'em from deal to showdown (Free)
  2. Poker hand rankings (Free)
  3. Pokerology poker lesson library (Free)

Review a tournament decision

Check the call price, prize-equity model, and format before a verdict.

  1. Pot odds step by step (Free)
  2. ICM basics (Free)
  3. Satellite strategy: equal-prize tournament decisions (Free)

Compare cash-game and Omaha study

Choose the exact game you play. These are separate starting points, not one transferable set of ranges.

  1. SplitSuit strategy and study resources (Mixed)
  2. PLO Mastermind article library (Free)
  3. Equity realization: why raw equity is not enough (Free)

Watch the thinking behind a hand

Use a creator account and a separate hand breakdown, not results alone.

  1. Brad Owen: inside the WPT World Championship (Free)
  2. Jaman Burton hand breakdown with Jonathan Little (Free)
  3. Lexy Gavin-Mather: blog and vlog companions (Free)

Find official event information

Start with the organizer, then check the specific schedule and structure.

  1. WSOP and Circuit schedule (Free)
  2. Thunder Valley poker information and events (Free)
  3. Wynn Las Vegas poker schedules and structures (Free)

Inspect tools and data

Read the manual, record format, or implementation before relying on outputs.

  1. PioSOLVER Quick Start documentation (Free)
  2. Poker Hand History file format specification (Free)
  3. Treys Python hand-evaluator repository (Free)

Looking for help rather than another study resource? See US gambling support or GamCare support for England and Scotland.

Put a resource to use

Choose by the question, not the biggest claim.

The study-tool guide distinguishes equity calculators, ICM models, solvers and trainers. The advice-reading guide helps compare articles, videos and charts without overlooking their assumptions. Try one private resource-check sheet rather than building a reading backlog.

Choosing an actual event? Start with the structure-sheet guide, then confirm the details with the official organizer.

How this directory grows

Broad coverage. A reason for every link.

Free describes the listed reading or resource. Mixed means free and paid material coexist. Paid identifies a commercial product or viewing library, even when its description is free. Features, registration, and regional access can change.

Each listing records its publisher, purpose, access type, suggested audience, and review date. Page read means the destination's public text or catalogue was inspected. It does not mean every article, paid course, download, calculation, or video was tested. Search index only means the official listing was confirmed but direct page reading was unavailable; that limitation is kept visible.

Discovery begins with original publishers, official rules and schedules, and references from useful articles. The next step is checking the destination, writing a specific description, removing duplicates and tracking parameters, and deciding where it belongs. Search results do not automatically become recommendations. New links are released in reviewed batches.

Some linked sites carry advertising, affiliate offers, gambling promotions, or paid upgrades. The links added here contain no affiliate or referral parameters. A listing is not a commercial partnership, a product endorsement, or permission to use a tool during play. Use study software after the session and follow the actual venue or operator's rules.

A large count is not evidence of being the best directory. Useful coverage, source diversity, clear access, working reader paths and honest review limits matter more. Schedules and products receive earlier review priority than stable explanations. A successful network response alone does not establish that the content is still relevant. A changed domain, new paywall, or broken destination requires review. No continuous link monitoring or automatic publication is implied by a review date.

Prepared with AI assistance. Descriptions are original summaries of public source pages. Reading and filtering here adds no custom analytics events or saved searches; the existing pageview privacy notice still applies. External sites use their own privacy and access policies when you open them.

Suggest a resource or report a broken linkRead this site's guidesBack to Poker

Download the complete directory as Markdown or download structured JSON. Both preserve individual review dates, access labels and cautions.

138 unique destinations on 72 hostnames. 119 free, 7 mixed, 12 paid. Hostnames are not a count of independent owners. Collection links reuse these listings and do not inflate the total.

For a suggestion, send the public URL and the question it answers. Do not send credentials, private hand records, or pirated material.
